description: Explains electrophilic aromatic substitution using resonance, inductive effects and product ratios; tests step order and compares directing strategies with cross-coupling.
tag_paths: Ring directing effects and competing electronic contributions

related_resources.reason: Ortho/para/meta substitution effects, activating and deactivating substituents.
Carbocation rearrangement, polyalkylation, acylation and limitations.
Defines preferential position and bond-formation direction.

historical_claims.anchor: The two neighboring carbons are ortho. The carbon directly opposite is para. The remaining two positions are meta.
Chlorobenzene is therefore generally deactivated yet ortho-para directing.
historical_claims.source_locator: Halogen inductive withdrawal and resonance donation.

historical_claims.anchor: Nitrobenzene is strongly deactivated; ordinary Friedel–Crafts alkylation generally fails on such rings.

authorship.scope: Original organic synthesis and selectivity lecture, scientific companion and source-linked catalog metadata.

background: Introductory organic molecular structure, carbonyls, bonding and reaction mechanisms. All additional specialist ideas are introduced in the narration.
readiness_checks: Why is chlorobenzene an ortho-para director but a deactivated substrate?
Why is reverse order of nitration and alkylation not equivalent?
